metrics.rationale: User requests '800-1500 nm 波段的高透射率' (high transmittance in 800-1500 nm band) to '尽可能完整地接收短波红外目标信号' (receive SWIR target signals as completely as possible).
User requests '200-400 nm 波段的高反射率' (high reflection in 200-400 nm band) to '尽可能反射紫外辐射' (reflect UV radiation as much as possible) and reduce stray light and UV damage.

standard.metric_rationale: These two metrics directly capture the user's dual-band requirement: maximize transmission in the SWIR signal band (800-1500 nm) while maximizing reflection in the UV rejection band (200-400 nm). I deliberately chose only 2 metrics (well under the 4-metric maximum) because the request has exactly two competing objectives—adding more metrics would dilute the scoring without covering additional user requirements. I used mean-based metrics rather than worst_case because the user specified band-level performance ('波段') rather than requiring every single wavelength to meet a threshold. I omitted angle_deg and polarization since the user specified '空气入射' (air incidence) without naming a specific angle or polarization state, so the default channel applies. I deliberately did not include absorption metrics because the user's request focuses on transmission and reflection performance, not thermal or loss considerations.
standard.formula_rationale: The user has two equally-stated goals: maximize SWIR signal reception (800-1500 nm transmittance) and maximize UV rejection (200-400 nm reflectance). The phrase '同时获得' (obtain simultaneously) indicates no priority between them, so both terms are added with equal weight. Each variable's maximize direction is respected by adding it directly—higher transmittance or higher reflectance both increase the score. No coefficients are introduced because the user gave no reason to favor one band over the other.
